research_item_name: TOP15 representative models and product lifecycle
source_title: Business-verified January-May Passenger Vehicle Monthly Validation Workbook, May sheet
May 2026 Fuel and New-Energy Passenger-Vehicle Sales Lists
evidence_excerpt: Workbook sedan TOP15 signals: Seagull 0.9664 x 10^4 units, -68.6% YoY; Qin PLUS 1.2150 x 10^4 units, -57.4%; Hongguang MINI EV 1.5039 x 10^4 units, -43.6%; Model 3 1.8583 x 10^4 units, +34.3% with rank movement of +57.

Workbook SUV TOP15 signals: Xingyue L 1.1277 x 10^4 units, -38.6%; Model Y 2.5108 x 10^4 units, broadly flat year on year; Leapmotor A10 and Li Auto i6 have no comparable year-on-year base; A10 rank movement is +14 and AITO M6 is +50.

Workbook MPV TOP15 signals: Buick GL8 0.5178 x 10^4 units, -55.3%; Denza D9 0.4330 x 10^4 units, -47.5%; WEY Gaoshan 0.5070 x 10^4 units, +61.7%; ZEEKR 009 0.1703 x 10^4 units, +44.4% with rank movement of +11.

A professional source reports that the 2026 ZEEKR 009 was launched on 19 May with a revised 900V architecture and an introductory price range after benefits. This is product-event evidence only, not proof of the model's May sales causality.
scope_and_caliber: The business workbook is the source of truth for this project's May TOP15 numbers and ranking changes. External articles may use a different retail/wholesale definition and are used only for product-event or competitive-context checks, never to overwrite workbook values.
metric_name: Estimated TOP15 sample year-on-year volume change
metric_value_and_unit: Sedan: Seagull estimated sample change -0.0211 million units; Qin PLUS -0.0164 million; Hongguang MINI EV -0.0116 million; Model 3 +0.0048 million
SUV: Xingyue L estimated sample change -0.0071 million; NIO ES8 +0.0113 million; new/no-comparable models are separately marked
MPV: Buick GL8 estimated sample change -0.0064 million; Denza D9 -0.0039 million; WEY Gaoshan +0.0019 million
metric_type: TOP15 sample data. Estimated year-on-year volume changes are calculated from workbook current volume and reported growth; they are selection signals, not whole-market contribution accounting.
comparison_period: May 2026 versus May 2025, except models explicitly marked as no comparable base in the workbook.
contribution_or_rank_change: The selected cases have the largest negative/positive estimated changes or material rank movements within each TOP15 sample. The full workbook contains 45 TOP15 records across sedan, SUV and MPV.
segment_definition: Sedan, SUV and MPV TOP15 lists from the May workbook. External publications can use different aggregation and scope, so direct number comparisons are prohibited.
structure_change: Sedan pressure is concentrated in multiple entry and A-class nameplates, SUV leadership includes several no-comparable models and MPV weakness is concentrated in established B-class nameplates while selected challengers grow.
representative_models: Sedan: Seagull, Qin PLUS, Hongguang MINI EV, Model 3
SUV: Xingyue L, Model Y, Leapmotor A10, Li Auto i6, AITO M6
MPV: Buick GL8, Denza D9, WEY Gaoshan, ZEEKR 009
lifecycle_event: ZEEKR 009: an external B-tier source reports a 19 May 2026 facelift/launch; causal contribution to May ranking remains unverified.
Leapmotor A10, Li Auto i6 and AITO M6: workbook has no year-on-year comparable base; classify as new/no-comparable monitoring cases until official launch and delivery evidence is attached.
Other selected models: no lifecycle event is asserted without a separately verified source.
overall_judgement: TOP15 evidence makes the market explanation more precise: the May category decline is not an abstract trend but is associated with several large negative sample movements in established sedan and MPV nameplates, while SUV ranking is being reshaped by no-comparable entrants and selected resilient models. Product-event evidence can prioritise what to investigate; it cannot turn a co-occurrence into a proven cause.
observed_fact: The workbook identifies Seagull, Qin PLUS, Hongguang MINI EV, Buick GL8, Denza D9 and Xingyue L as large negative TOP15 sample movements. It also identifies Model 3, WEY Gaoshan, ZEEKR 009 and multiple no-comparable SUV models as positive or ranking-change signals.
causal_mechanism: The workflow first selects models with material sample volume or rank movement, then requests evidence for product events. A product launch, facelift, price change or delivery event is treated as a candidate explanation only when its timing, market definition and model scope align with the internal signal. The evidence set currently confirms only the ZEEKR 009 launch event.
confidence_level: High for internal TOP15 facts; medium for external event facts; low for causal attribution except where additional official brand, price and delivery evidence is added.
alternative_explanations: Changes can be driven by product availability, fleet/corporate volume, export allocation, dealer inventory, incentives, regional supply, a prior-year base, model substitutions or statistical scope differences.
competitive_set: Within each vehicle category, selected TOP15 models should be compared to their direct class and powertrain peers rather than to the full passenger-vehicle market.
competitive_advantage_or_barrier: The current evidence indicates product-ramp and product-refresh events are worth tracking, but it does not establish configuration, brand or channel advantages for every selected model.
configuration_threshold: Only the 2026 ZEEKR 009 external source identifies product attributes, including a 900V architecture and revised intelligent-driving hardware. No cross-model configuration threshold has been validated.
pricing_and_profit_signal: The external ZEEKR 009 source reports a public price range after benefits. Transaction price, discount depth and profitability for the TOP15 sample are [uncertain].
target_user_segment: [uncertain] Model TOP15 data does not include buyer age, household, city tier, purchase type or usage scenario.
purchase_motivation_and_pain_points: [uncertain] Product-event articles may describe target scenarios, but no customer research has yet validated motives for the selected model changes.
purchase_barrier: [uncertain] Price, financing, charging access, dealer experience and delivery timing must be joined to model-level orders and cancellations before use in a causal conclusion.
channel_signal: For each selected model, track leads, test drives, orders, cancellations, deliveries, dealer inventory, transaction price and official product-event date alongside TOP15 movement.
opportunity_or_risk_grade: B research priority for selected SUV entrants and high-growth MPV cases; D watch for large negative established-model movements. Grades are research priorities, not product-entry approvals.
recommended_action: Use at most two to three selected TOP15 models per monthly deep-analysis page. State the measured movement first, add a verified event second, and label the causal link as pending unless evidence is sufficient.
regional_capacity_or_channel_action: Do not move capacity or set regional sales targets from national TOP15 rankings alone. Confirm regional allocation, delivery and inventory before action.
decision_condition_and_trigger: A model-level cause can enter a formal monthly report when the internal movement, an independently traceable event and at least one supporting channel or price signal agree on timing and scope.
next_verification: Create a controlled model-event ledger: official launch/facelift date, MSRP and transaction price, powertrain, configuration changes, delivery start, region, channel stock and user feedback for every selected TOP15 model.
data_quality_status: Passed for full TOP15 extraction and candidate selection; partially passed for product-event evidence; incomplete for model-level causal proof.
data_gap_or_conflict: External publications may state sales figures that differ from the internal workbook because of retail/wholesale scope, model aggregation or timing. The workflow therefore keeps internal figures authoritative and records external articles only as context.
claim_boundary: The results identify which models should be explained. They do not prove that a refresh, price action, competitor or user preference caused the observed model movement.
